title: How to Make Cannabis Cooking Oil (Canna Oil)
h1: How to Make Canna Oil for Cooking and Baking
metaDescription: How to make canna oil at home: which oils work best, decarbing, a simple stovetop method, potency per teaspoon, safe storage and easy ways to cook with it.
excerpt: A beginner-friendly canna oil method, from choosing coconut or olive oil to estimating strength per teaspoon and storing it safely.

body:
To make canna oil, decarb your cannabis, warm it gently in a cooking oil for a couple of hours, then strain. Here's how to make canna oil step by step, which oils work best, how to estimate strength per teaspoon and how to store it safely.

## Canna oil vs. store-bought cannabis oils

Homemade canna oil is a food oil infused with cannabis for cooking. It isn't the same as the oils on a dispensary menu:

- **RSO** is a thick, concentrated extract; see our [Rick Simpson Oil guide](/blog/what-is-rick-simpson-oil/).
- **Tinctures** are measured drops made with alcohol or oil; our [tincture guide](/blog/cannabis-tincture-guide/) explains them.
- **Vape oil** is a concentrate made for cartridges. Never cook with it, and never vape a cooking oil.

## Which oils infuse best

THC dissolves in fat, and cooking oils are almost pure fat, so any of them will carry it. Choose by flavor and by what you plan to cook:

| Oil | Flavor | Works well for |
|---|---|---|
| Coconut | Mild, or neutral if refined | Baking; firms up when chilled |
| Olive | Fruity, peppery | Dressings, drizzles, gentle sautés |
| Avocado | Mild | Sautés and roasting at moderate heat |
| Neutral, such as canola or sunflower | Very little | Any recipe where you don't want added flavor |

## Decarb first

Raw flower is mostly THCA, and a warm oil bath converts it slowly and unevenly. In lab tests, THCA conversion was still incomplete after 60 minutes below roughly 212°F, the range an oil infusion stays in. So give broken-up flower 30 to 45 minutes in a 240°F oven before it meets the oil. Our [decarb guide](/blog/cannabis-decarboxylation/) has the details.

## How to make canna oil: the method

The recipe card below has the full steps. In short, keep the oil and decarbed flower between 160 and 200°F, warm but not bubbling, for a two- to three-hour steep. A small saucepan on its lowest setting or a slow cooker on low both work. Need flower for your batch? Browse [your store's online menu](/shop/).

## Straining without the mess

Let the oil cool until it's warm, then pour it through a fine-mesh strainer lined with two layers of cheesecloth. Let it drip through on its own; squeezing pushes plant bits and a grassy taste into the oil.

## Dosing: estimating mg per teaspoon

A cup of oil holds 48 teaspoons. With 3.5 grams of 20% THC flower, the most THC you can get is 3.5 × 0.20 × 1,000 = 700 mg, or about 15 mg per teaspoon. Heat and the strained plant material keep the real number lower, and it can vary within the jar. That ceiling is above the 10 mg serving cap Michigan sets for store-bought adult-use edibles, so a full teaspoon could be a lot.

Begin with a quarter teaspoon, then let two full hours pass before thinking about more. For help finding your own starting point, see our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/).

## Storage and labeling

On its botulism prevention page, the CDC tells home cooks to refrigerate homemade oils made with garlic or herbs and to throw them away after 4 days. University of Georgia Extension adds that using dried ingredients doesn't make an infused oil safe on its own. Cannabis is a dried herb, so play it safe:

- **Refrigerate** canna oil in a sealed glass jar and use it within 4 days.
- **Freeze** the rest in small portions, such as an ice cube tray, then bag and label the cubes.
- **Never add** fresh garlic or herbs to the jar.
- **Label** it with the date and estimated strength, and keep it where kids and pets can't reach.

## Cooking with it: dressings, sautés and baking

- **Dressings:** whisk it into a vinaigrette or drizzle it over a finished dish.
- **Sautés:** use low to medium heat, or stir it in near the end, since long, high heat breaks THC down.
- **Baking:** swap it for part of the oil in brownies or muffins, and mix well.

Skip deep-frying, where the heat is high and the dose is hard to track. To bake with butter instead, see [how to make cannabutter](/blog/canna-butter/).

21+ only. Please consume responsibly.

faq.q: Which oil works best for canna oil, coconut or olive?
faq.a: Both work, because THC dissolves in any fat. Coconut oil suits baking and firms up when chilled, which makes it easy to measure. Olive oil brings a fruity, peppery flavor to dressings and drizzles. If you want the oil to disappear into a recipe, a neutral oil like canola or sunflower is the most flexible.

faq.q: Can you cook with canna oil at high heat?
faq.a: It's better not to. Lab research shows THC breaks down and is lost when heating runs hotter and longer, so hot, extended cooking wastes it. Use canna oil in no-heat dishes, gentle sautés or baking, or stir it in near the end, and skip deep-frying altogether.

faq.q: How long does homemade canna oil last?
faq.a: Keep it in the fridge and use it within 4 days, the CDC's guidance for homemade oils made with garlic or herbs. To keep it longer, freeze labeled portions and thaw only what you need. Never store it at room temperature, and never add fresh garlic or herbs to the jar.

faq.q: How strong is homemade canna oil?
faq.a: It depends on your flower and your method, so any number is an estimate. With 3.5 grams of 20% THC flower in a cup of oil, the ceiling is about 700 mg of THC, or roughly 15 mg per teaspoon. Real batches come in lower because of decarb and infusion losses. Start with a quarter teaspoon and wait at least two hours.

ingredients: 3.5 grams of cannabis flower, broken up by hand
1 cup of cooking oil, such as coconut, olive, avocado or a neutral oil
steps: Decarb first: spread the flower on a parchment-lined tray and give it 30 to 45 minutes in a 240°F oven, until it looks golden and feels dry. Cool it completely.
Put the oil and the decarbed flower in a small saucepan, a double boiler or a slow cooker.
Warm the mixture on the lowest setting so the oil holds around 160 to 200°F without bubbling. Keep it there for 2 to 3 hours, stirring from time to time.
Let the oil cool until it's just warm. Strain it through a double layer of cheesecloth into a heat-safe measuring cup and let it drip through on its own.
Pour the oil into a clean glass jar, write the date and estimated strength on the label and refrigerate it. Anything you won't use within 4 days goes into the freezer.
recipe.dosingNote: Here's the estimate: 3.5 g × 0.20 (for 20% THC flower) × 1,000 = 700 mg of THC at most, spread over 48 teaspoons, or roughly 15 mg per teaspoon. Your flower's true potency and the THC lost while decarbing and infusing decide the real figure, which will be lower and can vary within the jar. Begin with a quarter teaspoon and hold off on more for at least 2 hours. Label the jar and anything you cook with it, and keep both away from children and pets.
